liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **St. Stephen** (2 reviews): Calls the St. Stephen rare; says it wasn't played after 10-31-71 until 6-9-76; Phil's bass in this St. Stephen rumbles powerfully [6][7]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): A hot China Cat into Rider opens the second set [9]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): After St. Stephen and Drums, Jerry steers out of Not Fade Away into a strong jam [8]

## Setlist highlights

- **Curfew rap**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Sunshine Daydream [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-04-07.136892.sbd.GEMS.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 97 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd71-04-07.sbd.orf.119.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 97 min; rated 4.25/5 by 12 [2]. Said about its sound: Tape opens with audible Garcia guitar plug-in, gentle tuning noises and pedal sounds; The tape has a harsh cut around that jam, which the reviewer finds frustrating [6][8]
- **gd1971-04-07.sbd.cantor.gmb.96225.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 97 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [4]. Said about its sound: Reel changes are undetectable, apart from a cut in the jam after Drums leading into Not Fade Away [4]
- **gd1971-04-07.sbd.deibert.83301.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 17 songs; 96 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the soundboard sounds great and the band is well in tune [13]

## Around the show

- Reviewer suspects the show didn't open with Me and My Uncle because someone was changing a string [8]
- Comments report Jerry saying the show had to be kept short because of a venue curfew [16]
- Tuning after Sugar Magnolia and before China Cat suggests one continuous set rather than two [4]
- Jerry tells the audience the show must end after Johnny B. Goode because of the curfew [4]
- Reviewer ranks this show alongside Cornell as a milestone of the band's early years [6]
- Says the band seemed inspired at Boston Music Hall, citing September 1972 and late 1973 shows [9]
- The next night, with Dark Star, is more psychedelic; this first night is a rocker throughout [9]
- Reviewer thinks April 1971 shows stand comparable with May 1977 [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-04-07.136892.sbd.GEMS.flac16**: taped by PO and Stucco TINA Holmes; transferred by Jamie Waddell; source: Soundboard, unknown lineage; Sony L-750ESX-HFB Dynamicron EXCELLENT SUPER HIFI VIDEO CASSETTE->Sony SLO-1800 STEREO VIDEOCASSETTE RECORDER-> Sony PCM-601ESD… [1]
- **gd71-04-07.sbd.orf.119.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Leigh Orf; source: Soundboard (BB) [2]
- **gd1971-04-07.sbd.cantor.gmb.96225.flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Bill Koucky; source: 7" two track reel w@ 7 1/2 ips> PCM501ES @ 44.055 kHz CM501ES analog out > analog in PCM501ES analog out>Dat @ 48 kHz [4]
- **gd1971-04-07.sbd.deibert.83301.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Transferred by Tim Deibert 1-12-02; transferred by trailmix; source: 7" BBD Reel > PCM501ES > Fostex D5 > Fostex D5 optical S/PDIF out (Jace's tape) > disk [5]. Also: Original shn files from early 2002 never circulated; these were converted and fixed from files supplied by Tim Deibert [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1971-04-07 Wed Music Hall, Boston, MA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1478229000248/grateful-dead-1971-04-07-wed-music-hall) [19]
- Poster by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1971-04-07 Boston Music Hall, Boston, MA](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2018/07/grateful-dead-1971-04-07-boston-music_25.html) [20]
